extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies' NEPA practitioners, counsel, and NEPA document preparers/reviewers
extracted.subtask_short: implementing NEPA regulations for agency actions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory explanations for interpreting and applying revised NEPA regulatory definitions and exclusions (e.g., major Federal action, mitigation, scope, reasonable alternatives) when preparing or reviewing EISs, EAs, and related NEPA documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of 'minimal' Federal funding
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ did not adopt a numeric threshold for 'minimal Federal funding' and has not identified a threshold appropriate across Federal programs; agencies should evaluate whether funding is 'minimal' based on the specific factual context of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited case law exists and it does not define a clear threshold. Agencies must continue case-by-case factual analysis rather than apply a uniform dollar threshold; consider health of children, vulnerable populations, drinking water, environmental justice concerns, and similar circumstances when evaluating minimal funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for non-Federal actions with no or minimal Federal involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Federal actions with no or minimal Federal involvement where a Federal agency cannot control the outcome are excluded from the definition of 'major Federal action' (§1508.1(w)(2)(i)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces that major Federal actions are actions carried out by an agency, not non-Federal actions; minimal Federal involvement alone does not convert a non-Federal action into a Federal action. Examples: informal provision of information to a non-Federal party may not qualify as an agency action if the agency cannot control the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for funding assistance solely in the form of general revenue sharing funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding assistance solely in the form of general revenue sharing funds is excluded consistent with section 111(10)(B)(ii) of NEPA (§1508.1(w)(2)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion replaces the similar 2020 regulatory exclusion; CEQ received no substantive comments opposing this change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for loans, loan guarantees, or other financial assistance lacking sufficient agency control
rubrics_metrics.description: Loans, loan guarantees, or other forms of financial assistance where a Federal agency does not exercise sufficient control and responsibility over subsequent use of the assistance or the effects of the action are excluded consistent with section 111(10)(B)(iii) of NEPA (§1508.1(w)(2)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should evaluate specific actions providing financial assistance to determine whether the agency exercises sufficient control and responsibility; absence of such control may place the action within the exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory exclusion for certain SBA business loan guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain business loan guarantees provided by the Small Business Administration are excluded consistent with section 111(10)(B)(iv) of NEPA (§1508.1(w)(2)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ incorporates the statutory exclusion for SBA loan guarantees into the regulations and declines to expand similar blanket exclusions (e.g., for FSA) absent statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-level determination for FSA loans and similar programs
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ removed an explicit regulatory exclusion for Farm Service Agency (FSA) loan guarantees and directs FSA and other administering agencies to determine whether specific loan/guarantee actions meet the statutory/regulatory exclusion criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are best positioned to determine whether their loan programs involve sufficient agency control/responsibility to be excluded; CEQ declines to make blanket statements or broad categorical exclusions for such programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for bringing judicial or administrative enforcement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bringing judicial or administrative civil or criminal enforcement actions is excluded from the definition of 'major Federal action' (moved without change to §1508.1(w)(2)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This incorporation is consistent with the statutory text and longstanding agency practice; the exclusion encompasses an agency's decision to join a lawsuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for extraterritorial activities or decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities or decisions with effects located entirely outside the jurisdiction of the United States are excluded (moved without change to §1508.1(w)(2)(vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language aligns with section 111(10)(B)(vi) of NEPA; CEQ declines to remove this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for non-discretionary activities or decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-discretionary activities or decisions are excluded from NEPA applicability (moved without change to §1508.1(w)(2)(vii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some actions may be partially non-discretionary; agencies may appropriately exclude the non-discretionary aspects from NEPA analysis while treating discretionary aspects as potentially constituting major Federal actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality as a NEPA threshold (non-final agency actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ removed the separate regulatory exclusion for non-final agency actions from §1508.1 but treats finality as a threshold consideration under §1501.3; NEPA does not apply where a proposed activity or decision is not a final agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deletion is intended to have no substantive effect because §1501.3 provides that NEPA does not apply to non-final actions; agencies should use §1501.3 to determine finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for Tribal Nation-approved projects on trust or restricted lands with no or minimal Federal involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities or decisions for projects approved by a Tribal Nation that occur on or involve land held in trust or restricted status are excluded where such activities involve no or minimal Federal funding or other Federal involvement (§1508.1(w)(2)(viii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ added 'or minimal' for consistency with section 111 of NEPA. CEQ declines to broaden the exclusion (e.g., to all Tribal development). Categories typically not major Federal actions on trust lands are listed (e.g., transfer of operation/maintenance, social services, small service line agreements, certain Tribal regulatory approvals). CEQ declines to further define 'other Federal involvement' and leaves program-specific determinations to administering agencies; grants, contracts, cooperative agreements may be addressed in agency NEPA procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and application of 'mitigation' (mitigation hierarchy and authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ revised the definition of 'mitigation' to (1) use 'connection' rather than 'nexus'; (2) remove the sentence that 'NEPA does not mandate the form or adoption of any mitigation'; (3) add the clause 'in general order of priority' to introduce mitigation types (reflecting the mitigation hierarchy); and (4) clarify mitigation addresses 'adverse' effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'in general' qualifier allows flexibility so agencies may apply mitigation elements out of order when appropriate; agencies should prioritize avoidance and consider the full range of mitigation opportunities before selecting measures. Agencies must identify the legal authority for mitigation they rely on and should not rely on mitigation absent authority to ensure mitigation is performed. CEQ declined to add repetitive language requiring mitigation to be practicable/effective because those requirements are clear from regulations; CEQ defers to agencies on compensatory mitigation and use of third-party providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Intent (NOI) may include Environmental Assessments 'as applicable'
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ added 'environmental assessment' to the definition of 'notice of intent' but placed the qualifier 'as applicable' to make clear that issuing an NOI for an EA is discretionary and not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies have discretion to issue an NOI for an EA where appropriate to improve efficiency and effectiveness; adding EA to the definition does not create a new mandatory requirement to issue NOIs for EAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'page' and exclusions from page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ revised the definition of 'page' consistent with statute to exclude citations and appendices and retained the regulatory exclusions for explanatory maps, diagrams, graphs, tables, and other means of graphically displaying quantitative or geospatial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ reasons that excluding visual elements from the page count enhances comprehensibility of EAs and EISs. Agencies should limit visual elements in the body of the document to those that enhance comprehensibility and place additional information in appendices, per CEQ principles for clear and concise NEPA writing. CEQ rejects the argument that these exclusions circumvent statutory page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'participating Federal agency'
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ adds a definition of 'participating Federal agency' meaning 'a Federal agency participating in an environmental review or authorization of an action' consistent with section 111(8) of NEPA (§1508.1(dd)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No substantive comments were received; CEQ finalizes the definition as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of 'programmatic environmental document'
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ adds a definition of 'programmatic environmental document' consistent with section 111(11) of NEPA (§1508.1(ee)) and relies on §1501.11 for uses of programmatic analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declines to further clarify 'programmatic' in the definition because §1501.11 addresses the uses and distinguishing features (e.g., deferred decisions) of programmatic documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable alternatives — 'reasonable range' and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ retained the existing definition of 'reasonable alternatives' and did not revise it; agencies should consider alternatives that are 'technically and economically feasible' and evaluate a 'reasonable range of alternatives' that facilitates comparison of effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ may consider issuing further guidance; agencies commonly use the 'Forty Questions' as a starting point. CEQ rejects the notion that agencies must evaluate 'all' reasonable alternatives because that could be limitless; agencies should discuss alternatives dismissed from detailed analysis and explain the rationale; considerations include feasibility, cost, effectiveness, and public acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably foreseeable effects standard
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ retained the existing definition of 'reasonably foreseeable' using the ordinary person standard and declined requested changes (e.g., 'more likely than not' or replacing 'person of ordinary prudence' with 'prudent agency decision maker').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application is context-dependent; agencies must forecast effects to the extent they can either quantitatively or qualitatively within a reasonable range. Agencies are not required to 'foresee the unforeseeable.' The ordinary person standard is consistent with precedent and CEQ sees no practical problems with it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of NEPA analysis (including EAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ revised the definition of 'scope' to include Environmental Assessments and to define scope as both the range and breadth of the actions, alternatives, and effects to be considered in an EIS or EA (§1501.3(b) / §1508.1(kk)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of scope is a fact-specific analysis informed by the agency's statutory authority and control/responsibility over the activity. CEQ struck non-definitional tiering language from the definition because tiering is addressed elsewhere (§1501.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant effects defined as adverse effects and significance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ adds a definition of 'significant effects' to mean adverse effects identified by an agency as significant based on the criteria set forth in §1501.3(d); beneficial effects are not 'significant effects' for purposes of triggering an EIS (§1508.1(mm)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach means an agency need not prepare an EIS if a proposed action's effects are exclusively beneficial. However, irrespective of required level of review, agencies must analyze both adverse and beneficial effects in NEPA documents if they are reasonably foreseeable. CEQ revised §1501.3(d) in tandem for clarity on applying context and intensity factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiering definition cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ revised the definition of 'tiering' to cross-reference the process set forth in §1501.11 (§1508.1(oo)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tiering procedures and uses are addressed in §1501.11; CEQ did not expand the definitional text beyond linkage to that section.
